title: Fake Node-Based Perception Poisoning Attacks against Federated Object Detection Learning in Mobile Computing Networks
problem: Federated learning systems for object detection are vulnerable to poisoning attacks, with existing methods either requiring compromise of majority participants or suffering from poor attack success rates.
motivation: Securing federated learning in mobile edge computing is critical as distributed training systems are exposed to adversarial attacks with potentially undetected malicious influence.
method: FNPPA poisons local training data and injects multiple fake nodes into the federated aggregation process. The fake nodes participate in model aggregation to amplify poisoned updates, making the poisoned model more likely to overwrite clean updates. The attack selectively targets specific objects while preserving normal detection on non-target objects.
key_novelty: Using fake node injection in federated aggregation to amplify poisoned local updates with significantly lower attacker cost than methods requiring majority participant compromise.
contributions: Proposes FNPPA attack combining local data poisoning with fake node injection for federated object detection
Demonstrates superior attack impact on target objects compared to state-of-the-art methods
Achieves selective object poisoning while maintaining normal detection of other objects
Reduces attacker cost compared to existing poisoning attack approaches
primary_theme: Adversarial attacks on federated object detection
